public_rationale: Zitron's first point is hedged: outside OpenAI and Anthropic, the three companies 'do not appear' to be growing revenue significantly. He bases it on backlog (RPO) and sets no threshold. Microsoft's own figures cut against it for Microsoft: backlog outside OpenAI grew 28% and 26% year over year in the quarters ending December 2025 and March 2026. But those figures include Anthropic's $30 billion commitment and are yearly, not the quarter-over-quarter view he uses. Google and Amazon give no split by customer. His second point, that the only way to get this revenue is to fund the labs, has no clear public test. Because the claim is hedged and has no threshold, I do not score it either way.
limitations: Hedged wording with no stated threshold.
Only Microsoft splits out OpenAI, and nobody splits out Anthropic.
The evidence is backlog, while his words say revenues.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Outside of OpenAI and Anthropic, Microsoft, Google and Amazon do not appear to be significantly increasing their revenues, and the only way to get that revenue is to feed money to one or both of those companies.

statement.excerpt: That was a lot of numbers, so let me make it simpler: outside of OpenAI and Anthropic, these three companies do not appear to be significantly increasing their revenues, and the only way to get that revenue is to feed money to one or both of these companies.

from_speaker: do not appear to be significantly increasing their revenues
the only way to get that revenue is to feed money to one or both of these companies
our_interpretation: In context the first part rests on remaining performance obligations (RPO, contracted future revenue) for calendar Q4 2025 to Q1 2026. It says growth outside OpenAI and Anthropic does not appear significant. It is hedged ('do not appear') and gives no threshold for 'significantly', so I treat it as an impression, not a firm figure.
The second part is firmer. The plain reading is that the three hyperscalers win OpenAI and Anthropic revenue only by investing in or funding those companies themselves.
Period: calendar Q4 2025 through Q1 2026, the quarters he discusses.
criteria.support_condition: Company disclosures showing little or no growth in revenue or backlog once OpenAI and Anthropic are removed, and records showing that each large OpenAI or Anthropic compute deal with these firms depended on the hyperscaler's own investment in that lab.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Company disclosures showing clearly strong growth in revenue or backlog outside OpenAI and Anthropic at all three firms, together with large OpenAI or Anthropic compute deals these firms won without investing in the lab.
